addition.title: Left-to-Right Addition
addition.text: Add the largest place values first (tens, then ones) to build the total in your head naturally.

addition.title: Round and Compensate
addition.text: When adding a number close to a multiple of 10, round up and subtract the extra at the end.

addition.title: Making Tens
addition.text: Borrow a small number from one addend to round the other to a clean multiple of 10.

subtraction.title: Add Up Instead
subtraction.text: Instead of borrowing backwards, count forwards from the subtracted number to the target.

subtraction.title: Round and Compensate
subtraction.text: Round the subtracted number to a clean multiple of 10, then add back the difference.

subtraction.title: Same Change Rule
subtraction.text: Add the same amount to both numbers to turn the subtrahend into a clean multiple of 10.

multiplication.title: Multiply by 5 Shortcut
multiplication.text: To multiply any number by 5, divide it by 2 and multiply by 10 (or append a zero).

multiplication.title: Split and Distribute
multiplication.text: Split a 2-digit number into tens and ones, multiply each separately, and sum the products.

multiplication.title: Double and Halve
multiplication.text: Double one factor and halve the other to simplify the mental calculation.

division.title: Divide by 5 Shortcut
division.text: To divide by 5, double the dividend and divide by 10 (drop the zero or shift the decimal).

division.title: Factor the Divisor
division.text: Break composite divisors into smaller prime factors and divide in two quick steps.

division.title: Partial Quotients
division.text: Split the dividend into large friendly multiples of the divisor.

squares.title: Numbers Ending in 5
squares.text: Multiply the tens digit by (tens digit + 1), then append 25 to the end.

squares.title: Base 50 Method
squares.text: For numbers near 50 with difference d: the hundreds are (25 ± d) and the end is d².

squares.title: Difference of Squares
squares.text: Calculate a² using (a - d)(a + d) + d² by picking d that rounds to a multiple of 10.

cubes.title: Check the Last Digit
cubes.text: Cubes of 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 0 keep their ending digit; 2 pairs with 8, and 3 pairs with 7.

cubes.title: Stepwise Cubing (n² × n)
cubes.text: Recall or compute the square first, then multiply once more by n using distribution.

cubes.title: Cubes of Multiples of 10
cubes.text: Cube the non-zero digit and append three zeroes for every zero in the base.

squareRoots.title: Last Digit Clues
squareRoots.text: Look at the last digit: ending in 1 means the root ends in 1 or 9; ending in 9 means 3 or 7.

squareRoots.title: Bracket Between Tens
squareRoots.text: Identify which multiples of 10 surround the square, then test the midpoint ending in 5.

squareRoots.title: Roots of Numbers Ending in 25
squareRoots.text: If a square ends in 25, the root ends in 5. The leading digits equal n × (n + 1).

cubeRoots.title: Unique Last Digit
cubeRoots.text: Unlike squares, every digit 0-9 produces a unique ending digit in cubes (2<->8, 3<->7, others unchanged).

cubeRoots.title: Strip Last Three Digits
cubeRoots.text: Ignore the hundreds, tens and ones. Match the remaining thousands to the nearest cube below it.
cubeRoots.example: ∛4096: ignore 096; thousands = 4 (between 1³=1 and 2³=8, tens is 1). Last digit is 6 -> 16

cubeRoots.title: Master Cubes up to 10
cubeRoots.text: Memorizing 1³ through 10³ allows finding any perfect cube root up to 1,000,000 instantaneously.

exponents.title: Powers of 2 Chain
exponents.text: Double continuously to reach high powers of 2 mentally.

exponents.title: Split Exponents (a^(m+n))
exponents.text: Split a tricky exponent into the sum of two familiar exponents and multiply the results.

exponents.title: Power of a Power ((a^m)^n)
exponents.text: Rewrite even powers as squares of known values.
